items.followUp: Differentiate between accuracy and precision in scientific observations.

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics without numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that these observations are descriptive and non-numerical.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations involve measurements expressed numerically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these observations are measured or expressed in numbers.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics and are not expressed numerically.
Quantitative observations involve measurements and are expressed in numbers.
followUp：Give one example each of a qualitative and a quantitative observation.

items.followUp: What are the functions of plasmodesmata in plant cells?

rubric.why: Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic channels passing through the walls between neighbouring plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as channels connecting the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells through their walls.

rubric.why: These connections enable substances and signals to pass between neighbouring cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they facilitate transport or communication between adjacent cells.

modelAnswer: Plasmodesmata are narrow cytoplasmic channels that pass through the cell walls of neighbouring plant cells.
They connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells and allow transport and communication between them.

items.followUp: Name two substances transported by phloem.

rubric.why: Phloem carries prepared food, especially sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the movement of food or sugars from leaves to other parts of the plant.

rubric.why: Phloem transports dissolved food substances, including sugars and amino acids, throughout the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying amino acids or sugars as substances transported by phloem.

modelAnswer: Phloem transports prepared food, especially sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
It also transports dissolved food substances such as sugars and amino acids throughout the plant.

items.followUp: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification, and what kingdoms did it include?

rubric.why: Ernst Haeckel proposed the three-kingdom classification in 1866.
The system added Protista to the earlier kingdoms Plantae and Animalia; unicellular organisms were placed in Protista.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the three kingdoms or explaining that Protista was added for unicellular organisms.

modelAnswer: Ernst Haeckel proposed the three-kingdom classification in 1866.
It classified organisms into Plantae, Animalia and Protista; unicellular organisms were placed in Protista.

items.followUp: What happens to the amount of DNA and the number of chromosomes during S phase?

rubric.why: DNA is replicated during the synthesis (S) phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is copied or replicated.

rubric.why: DNA content doubles as each chromosome forms two sister chromatids, while chromosome number remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA content doubles or sister chromatids form, while chromosome number remains the same.

modelAnswer: During the S phase, DNA is replicated.
The DNA content doubles and each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids, but the chromosome number remains unchanged.

items.followUp: How do germ-line cells give rise to gametes?

rubric.why: Somatic cells make up the body and are not the cells that produce gametes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying somatic cells as body cells.

rubric.why: Germ-line cells give rise to gametes, generally through meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that germ-line cells produce gametes.

modelAnswer: Somatic cells are the body cells that form the tissues and organs of an organism.
Germ-line cells give rise to gametes, usually by meiosis.

items.followUp: How is the cell plate formed during cytokinesis in plant cells?

rubric.why: During plant-cell cytokinesis, microtubules between the daughter nuclei form the phragmoplast, which guides cell-plate formation.
rubric.description: Formation and role of the phragmoplast
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the phragmoplast or microtubules between the daughter nuclei and their role in guiding the process.

rubric.why: Golgi-derived vesicles gather and fuse at the cell centre to form the cell plate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vesicles gather or fuse at the centre to form the cell plate.

modelAnswer: During cytokinesis, microtubules between the daughter nuclei form the phragmoplast.
Golgi-derived vesicles gather and fuse along it at the centre of the cell to form the cell plate.

items.followUp: Name the two photosystems and state where they are located.

rubric.why: A photosystem is a group of light-absorbing pigments associated with proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a photosystem as a pigment-and-protein complex, or as a group of light-absorbing pigments.

rubric.why: Photosystems are embedded in thylakoid membranes, where they absorb light energy for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving their thylakoid-membrane location or stating that they absorb light energy.

modelAnswer: Photosystems are groups of light-absorbing pigments, including chlorophyll, associated with proteins.
They are embedded in the thylakoid membranes and absorb light energy for photosynthesis.
